issue_context.title: systemd-boot hangs if YubiKey is present
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
> systemd 245 (245.5-2-manjaro)

**Used distribution**
 > Manjaro 20.0.1

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > Boot screen interactivity and regular progress.

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**

 If a YubiKey is (already) connected at boot time, systemd-boot hangs. If a timeout is set, the menu is shown but the counter immediately freezes; if a timeout isn't set, the screen stays blank. In both cases the system can't be interacted with apart from forcibly powering it off.

**Steps to reproduce the problem**

1. Boot with a YubiKey in an USB port.
2. The system hangs at systemd-boot's menu.

I can reproduce this behavior with both a YK 4 Nano (`1050:0407`) and a YK Neo (`1050:0116`). Different ports and/or hubs do not seem to be affecting the result; I don't have other devices causing this issue at hand.

---

<details><summary>/boot/loader/loader.conf</summary>

```
timeout 3
console-mode keep
default manjarolinux5.6
```
</details>

<details><summary>/etc/fstab</summary>

```
# /dev/mapper/cryptroot
UUID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx	/         	ext4      	rw,noatime	0 0
# /dev/nvme0n1p1
UUID=xxxx-xxxx      	/boot     	vfat      	rw,relatime,fmask=0022,dmask=0022,codepage=437,iocharset=iso8859-1,shortname=mixed,utf8,errors=remount-ro	0 0
/swapfile       	none      	swap      	defaults,pri=-2	0 0
```
</details>

comments: hmm, so i doubt there#s anything we can do about that. usb drivers for keyboards and stuff are handled inside the firmware. Is this reproducible on other systems? Have you tried updating your firmware?

Unfortunately I don't have any other system that I can equip with the same sw stack, and I've already updated my BIOS to the most recent version publicly available. Live mediums using GRUB seem to be booting fine though.

The same problem occurs on my notebbok (HP Spectre 15-df0xxx) when there is a usb keyboard connected, it appears only with sd-boot and grub but not with microsoft's BCD.
The only way to boot is to disconnect the usb keyboard or press F9 (show firmware boot order menu) and select the boot loader from the menu.

Is it possible to disable USB devices from sd-boot and automatically boot into default OS without showing menu? (it is not a solution but a good compromise)
FYI - I have the same problem with `systemd 245 (245.4-4ubuntu3.6)` on an HP Spectre 14-ea0023dx
Same issue with `systemd 249-3` on an HP Spectre 15-df0xxx (Arch) with an external keyboard connected
Something is definitely off in the way HP's firmware handles USB devices but their customer support hasn't been willing to acknowledge that so far.

> Does this branch fix this?
> https://github.com/medhefgo/systemd/tree/boot

Hi, I have tested this patch and it doesn't fix the problem.

this https://github.com/eliadevito/systemd/commit/0e3aafc5b9c2f64ae37db4c1615ef1370ec54251 has fixed the probnlem on my HP Spectre 15-df0xxx
from what I understand it looks like sd-boot freeze on this line 

`err  = uefi_call_wrapper(ST->ConIn->ReadKeyStroke, 2, ST->ConIn, &k);`

removing it fix the freeze but the arrow keys doesn't work correctly.

The solution should instead be here:

on boot.c insdie efi_main() function we have this 
```

err = console_key_read(&key, FALSE);

if (err == EFI_NOT_READY) {
        uefi_call_wrapper(BS->Stall, 1, 100 * 1000);
        err = console_key_read(&key, FALSE);
}
```
 
IMO the uefi_call_wrapper(ST->ConIn->ReadKeyStroke, 2, ST->ConIn, &k) call should be return EFI_NOT_READY 
until firmware not ready instead it causes the system to freeze, differently the uefi_call_wrapper(TextInputEx->ReadKeyStrokeEx, 2, TextInputEx, &keydata) call seem to return it (I suppose) in fact by adding the return in case of error sd-boot don't freeze anymore and work very well with or without an external keyboard connected.

The only thing is that only the notebook's built-in keyboard works and not the external one but it shouldn't be such a big problem.

I have tested this on Fedora 34, if someone want to test it I have created a copr repository with patched systemd
https://copr.fedorainfracloud.org/coprs/scorpionit/systemd_HP/
I've reworked my branch. Does it work for you with that?

> I've reworked my branch. Does it work for you with that?

I have tested your reworked branch and unfortunately  it doesn't work,

`if (TextInputEx && !EFI_ERROR(uefi_call_wrapper(BS->CheckEvent, 1, TextInputEx->WaitForKeyEx))) {`

this conditions is always false when you call console key_read with wait variable setted to false and don't press any key causing the fallback code to execute witch consequently firmware hang
Am I getting this right: with wait set to true this code works?

> Am I getting this right: with wait set to true this code works?

Yes, if I force wait variable to true it works
Perfect! I've updated my branch which sidesteps the whole issue. It *should* work.
Also, if you force wait to true and force using ConIn instead of TextInputEx, does that also work?

> Perfect! I've updated my branch which sidesteps the whole issue. It _should_ work.

With these latest changes, no hang at all.
The only remain bug is for print_status(SHIFT+P) that don't wait to press a key to continue, but this should be solved by disabling the timer when the wait variable is true (I assume).

> Also, if you force wait to true and force using ConIn instead of TextInputEx, does that also work?

No, the ConnIn cause hang in all case

Can you please add a fix for print_status() an submit this as PR?

Thanks a lot for you work, good job.
I'll make a PR with a ton of other sd-boot goodies containing a fix for this in the next week or two.
Please double check that it works with my PR.

One last thing: could you slap this line at the top of console_key_read() of the latest git main and tell me if any of them say no at runtime? I feel like your firmware might be giving us null pointers here.

`log_error_stall(L"ConIn: %s
ConInHandle: %s
ReadKeyStroke: %s
WaitForKey: %s", yes_no(!!ST->ConIn), yes_no(!!ST->ConsoleInHandle), yes_no(!!ST->ConIn && !!ST->ConIn->ReadKeyStroke), yes_no(!!ST->ConIn && !!ST->ConIn->WaitForKey));`

review_comments:
This essentially removes the fallback to ReadKeyStroke below. The patch as such doesn't make sense. It solves the case when ReadKeyStrokeEx works but ReadKeyStroke is buggy, but will break systems where ReadKeyStrokeEx is not available.

I we are calling ReadKeyStroke correctly (and I assume we are), then the only options seems to be to avoid calling ReadKeyStroke on HP. (We print FirmwareVendor in print_status(), so we could do a check against this string here.)

From the comment in the source I had seemed to understand that the fallback mode was necessary 
only when the ReadKeyStrokeEx works but doesn't return any key, 
so I thought that the case which 'keypress' <= 0 was enough.

Anyway I will take a look to FirmwareVendor in print_status() and update this PR

sadly @medhefgo patch doesn't work, so I took a look to FirmwareVendor and it don't seem a viable solution, the FirmwareVendor string don't contains "HP" but "American Megatrends" so we can't use it to determine if sd-boot is running on an HP machine.

At this point, a configuration option to disable the fallback call can be considered an acceptable idea?
